Ariidae is a karyologically diverse fish family.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ariids have a diploid number ranging from 2 to 7 chromosomes, a fundamental number ranging from 54 to 60 and a karyotypic formula varying from 2M + 2A to 14M + 18ST + 4A.

the karyotypes of the three ariids studied here, as well as the other species previously reported, are characterized by the absence of sex chromosomes, the occurrence of a high number of telocentrics, the presence of NORs, and the absence of heterochromatin blocks.

the karyotypes of the three ariid species studied herein have a high diploid number, a low fundamental number (NF) and a large number of telocentric chromosomes, which is a characteristic of the Siluriformes.

the cytogenetic analysis is an important tool for species identification and for the understanding of the karyotype evolution within the fish family Ariidae.
